decisive_items: progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas involving the mandibular bodies, angles, ascending rami, and the maxillary tuberosities
response.rationale: Bilateral symmetric jaw swelling in a young child with multilocular radiolucencies and intact oral mucosa is classic for Cherubism. Central giant cell granuloma can appear multilocular but is typically solitary, while brown tumor is contradicted by unremarkable hematologic tests.

rejected.why: Multilocular jaw lesions can occur in brown tumor, but routine hematologic tests were unremarkable, arguing against hyperparathyroidism.
Multilocular radiolucencies are shared, but the symmetric bilateral jaw involvement and young age favor Cherubism over central giant cell granuloma.
